segments.label: United States v. South-Eastern Underwriters Ass’n, syllabus ¶ 1
segments.text: 1. A fire insurance company which conducts a substantial part of its business transactions across state lines is engaged in "commerce among the several States" and subject to regulation by Congress under the Commerce Clause. P. 539.

segments.label: United States v. South-Eastern Underwriters Ass’n, syllabus ¶ 2
segments.text: 2. A conspiracy to restrain interstate trade and commerce by fixing and maintaining arbitrary and noncompetitive premium rates on fire and allied lines of insurance, and a conspiracy to monopolize interstate trade and commerce in such lines of insurance, held violations of the Sherman Antitrust Act. P. 553.

segments.label: United States v. South-Eastern Underwriters Ass’n, syllabus ¶ 3
segments.text: 3. Congress did not intend that the business of insurance should be exempt from the operation of the Sherman Act. Pp. 553, 560.
